title: Real Estate: Cheap Leads But Zero Call Pickups
story: A real estate builder in Noida is running lead ads for 2BHK luxury apartments starting at ₹75 Lakhs. Leads are coming in cheap at ₹90 each, but the sales director is furious: '85% of these leads say they never filled any form or hang up immediately!'

table: Bold in video hook and headline

steps.prompt: What caused so many people to claim they 'never filled any form'?
options: The 'More Volume' instant form auto-filled their profile details and submitted on an accidental click without clear price disclosure
steps.explain: Default auto-fill forms allow users to submit in two accidental taps without even reading what property was advertised.

steps.prompt: What changes must you implement immediately in Ads Manager?
options: Put '₹75 Lakhs Onwards' prominently in the headline, switch to 'Higher Intent' form, and add mandatory custom dropdowns: 'Budget: ₹75L-₹1Cr' and 'Buying Timeline'
Run ads only in the USA
steps.explain: Placing price front-and-center filters out window shoppers who cannot afford ₹75 Lakhs, while mandatory dropdowns ensure intentional submission.

finalQuestion: CPL will likely rise from ₹90 to ₹350 after this change. How will you explain this to the builder?
keyPoints: Explain that ₹90 leads were costing sales team wasted hours calling fake prospects
Cost per Site Visit and qualified buyer cost is what actually determines ROI
Fewer, higher-intent leads produce more actual property sales
modelAnswer: I explain that paying ₹90 for leads who hang up wastes your sales team's payroll and morale. By adding price transparency and qualifying questions, CPL will rise to ₹350, but 70% of those leads will answer calls and schedule site visits. 10 qualified site visits at ₹350 CPL generate far more booked apartments than 100 accidental clicks at ₹90.
